caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 54 of 1982
lawyer:
Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, with Mr. M. Golam  Rabbain, Advocates ------ for the Appellant. 
Mr. Mansur Habib, Advocate ------ for the Respondents.
parties:
Kamar Begum Roy ------ Appellant
Vs.
M. Khalilur Rahman ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-respondent No.1, M. Khalilur Rahman, instated O.C. Suit No. 198 of 1976 which was renumbered as O.C. Suit No. 40 of 1978 against the appellant and 9 others for declaration of his title simpliciter in the suit land measuring 23.18 acres described in the schedules Ka, Kha, Ga and Gha to the plaint on the allegations, inter-alia, that the suit properties originally belonged to Patia Four-Anna Raj Estate within the District of Rajshahi that the plaintiff used to serve as inspector of the said patia Four-Annas Estate; that the proprietor of  the said Patia 'Estate, Rani Sureswari Devi being satisfied  with the work of the plaintiff setteled the suit land with him on the 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B.S. at a total rental of Tk. 64/9/3 pies that since the pattan the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land on payment of rent to the ex-landlord as well as to the Court of Wards on receipt of dakhilas that during the S.A. operation the suit land was recorded in the name of the ex-Landlord Rani Sureswari Devi in S.A . Khatian No. 97, 137, 138 and 142, that the plaintiff thereafter filed O.C. Suit Nos. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63, and 306/63 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi, against Rani Sureswari Devi in respect of the aforesaid Four Katians, that after the death of Rani Sureswari Devi her daughters were supporting the plaintiffs case but the plaintiff had to withdraw those suits later on in view of the provision of East Pakistan Ordinance No.1 of 1964; that the defendant No.1 filed a petition under section 50 of the State Acquistion and Tenancy Act before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi claiming herself to be the wife of late Raja Naresh Narayan Roy being miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1965 to insert her name in the aforesaid four khatains after striking out the name of Rani Sureswari Devi therefrom and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi by his order dated 28.10.64 and 2.12.65 allowed the two miscellaneous cases directing to record the name of Rani Sureswari Devi from the four khatians, that the defendant No.1 was importer and she lost the case No.33 of 1950 before the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and also before the Member, Board of Revenue in her attempt to register her name in the relevant touzis owned by the Patia four Anas Zaminder; that thereafter defendant No. 1 filed O.C. Suit No. 45 of 1951 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi claiming her title in the properties of Patia four-anas Estate and she lost upto the Appellate Court, that Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy never married defendant No.1 and he never embraced Islam and he died as Hindu and his dead body was burnt according to Hindu custom; that the suit properties were enlisted as enemy properties by the Additional Deputy commissioner, Rajshahi and the Assistant Custodian of the enemy properties but on the ejection of the plaintiff the Asstt. Custodian released the properties in favour of the plaintiff; that there were many criminal cases between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 wherein she admitted the title of the plaintiff; that the order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.). Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 under Section 50 of the State Acquistion and Tenancy Act substituting the name of defendant No.1 in place of Rani Sreswari Devi in the aforesaid S. A. khatians relating to the suit lands have cloud upon the title of the plaintiff over the suit lands and that the cause of action of the suit arose on 28.4.72 when the defendant No.1 claimed her title in the suit lands and hence this suit for simple declaration. 

 3. The appellant-defendant No.1 contested the suit denying the material averment made in the plaint and contending inter-alia, that the plaintiff had no cause of action for the suit; that the suit was not maintainable in its present form, the same being hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act; that the suit was barred by limitation; that the plaintiff never took settlement of the suit properties and if he produced any document in support of the so-called Patia Zaminder then all such documents were forged, spurious, fictitious and anti-dated; that it was not true that the defendant No. 1 was not married wife of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy alias Nuru Nabi Roy Chowdhury, that Raja Naresh Narayan Roy embraced Islam and adopted the name of Raja Nurun Nabi Roy Chowdhury and married defendant No. 1, that on the death of her husband the defendant inherited the suit properties and other properties left by her husband, that as Rani Sureswari Devi acquire no interest in the Suit properties the entry of her name in the S. A. Khatian was illegal and void that having no title and possession in the suit land the present suit of the plaintiff was liable to be dismissed. 

 "Ext. 8 and Ext. 9 show that the order in Misc. Case No. 9/64 and 5/65 U/S. 50 of the E. B. S. and T. Act by Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi was set aside by the Commissioner and the Member, Board of Revenue. So in view of Ext. 8 and 9 it is found that the name of Rani Sureswari Devi was restored in S. A. Khatians of the suit property." 

 11. In the meantime the plaintiff-respondent instituted four suits in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Rajshahi being other suit No. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63 and 306/63 praying for declaration of his title in the suit land on the ground that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi in S. A. Khatians 97, 137, 138 and 142 on the allegation that he took settlement of the suit land on the 23rd of Aswin, 1354 B. S. from Rani Sureswari Devi but the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. It further appears that during the pendencey of those suits the plaintiff and Rani Sureswari Devi filed two petitions of compromise in O. C. Suit No. 314/63 and 261/63 and on the death of Sureswari Devi another set of petitions of compromise by the plaintiff-respondent and the daughters of Sureswari Devi were filed but the plaintiff ultimately withdrew both the suits on 23.11.65 on the ground that the suits were not maintainable without any prayer for consequential relief in the shape of confirmation of possession. So far as O. C. Suit Nos. 306/63 is concerned, both the suits were barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It further appears that the plaintiff filed two appeals namely, Title Appeal No. S. 148 and 149 of 1965 against the order of dismissal of the latter two suits and at the appellants stage the plaintiff also filed two applications for withdrawal of the suits on the self same ground which were allowed (Exts. 4(G) and 4(H). It may be mentioned here that the plaint, the petition for compromise, the petition for adjournment etc. of O. C. suits 314/63 and 261/63 have been marked as Ext. 18 to 18(L). 

 12. The appellant, defendant No. 1 filed an application under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was numbered as Misc. Case No. 9 of 1964 praying for recording her name in S. A. khatian 97 in place of the name of Sureswari Devi and the Addl. Deputy commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi by his order dated 28.10.64 allowed her application and directed to insert the name of Kamar Begum in S. A. kahtian 97 of mouza Patia in place of Sureswari Devi. Against this order of the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Rajshahi Panna Devi and 3 others, daughters of Sureswari Devi filed a petition for review which was rejected by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi by his order dated 22.12.62 (Ext. B(1). Similarly the appellant filed another application under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, being Misc. Case No. 5 of 1965, for inserting her name in S. A. Khatians 137, 138 and 142 of mouza Patia in place of Sureswari Devi and this application was also allowed by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi by his order dated 2.11.65 Accordingly the four S. A. Khatians were corrected in the name of the appellant. 

 13. Thus in view of the above discussions the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that four O. C. suits were compromised now that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land Rani Sureswari Devi as quoted earlier was wrong. Also the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the orders passed in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 were set aside by the Commissioner, Rajshahi Division and the Member, Board of Revenues restoring the name of Rani Sureswari Devi in the four S. A. khatians was wrong. 

 14. Now coming to the present suit, the plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of his title simpliciter in the suit land without any prayer for consequential relief in the form of confirmation/recovery of possession of the self same allegation that he took settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi. Although in the Plaint it has been stated that the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land from Rani Sureswari Devi by dakhilas dated 23rd Aswin, 1354 B. S. but in his deposition as P. W. 1 he stated that he took settlement of the suit land by four amalnamas and he filed the amalnamas Ext, 1 to 1(c), in support of his statement. He also alleged in the plaint that because of the promulgation of Disturb Persons (Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1964 he had to withdraw the four O.C. suits filed in 1963; but as has been mentioned earlier the four O.C. suits were withdrawn on the ground that the suits for simple declaration without any preyer for consequential relief were not maintainable. In the present suit the plaintiff introduced the story of promulgation of Ordinance I of 1964 which provides that no suit for declaration of title be instituted or proceeded with without the permission of the authorised officer. The Plaintiff could have obtained the permission from the authorised officer and proceeded with those suits. It appears that the real difficulty was that the appellant by virtue of the orders passed in her favour in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 got her name inserted in the four khatians in place of Sureswari Devi and during the pendency of the above mentioned four O.C. suits she got herself added as defendant in the suits. That seems to be the real reason for the plaintiff to withdraw those suits. 

 16. Now the question is whether Rani Sureswari Devi at all inherited the suit properties from Raja Naresh Narayan Roy and she was competent to grant the alleged settlement. As has been noticed earlier originally the suit land was recorded in the four S. A. khatians in the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. The appellant by obtaining orders of Addl. Deputy commissioner (Rev.), Rajshahi in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 got her name inserted in those khatians in place of the name of Rani Sureswari Devi. The S.A. khatians were accordingly corrected and in the subsequent R.S. khatians the suit land was recorded in the name of the appellant. As the appellant got herself added as party defendant in O.C. Suit Nos. 314/63, 261/63, 262/63 and 306/63, the plaintiff had to withdraw those suits on the ground that the suit for simple declaration for title without any prayer for consequential relief were not maintainable. In the present case, apart from the plaintiff, there are seven other P.Ws. The plaintiff as P.W.1 stated about his possession in the suit land. P.W.2 Merajuddin stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land for 14/15 years. He further stated that he came from India 15/15 years ago and admitted that he cannot say about the area the suit land. P.W.3 Abdul Majid stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land. He also came to Patia from India 25/26 years ago and the suit land is 1½ miles away from his house. This P. W. 3 also stated that the defendant No. 1 was residing in the Kacharibari of the Estate, although the Judgment of the Criminal case which was also marked as Ext. A shows that the defendant No.1 was acquitted for trespassing into the house of Raja Naresh Narayan Roy in 1950 and P.W.1 admitted in his cross-examination that the house in which the defendant No.1 is residing now belonged to Raja Naresh Narayan Roy. P.W.4 stated that the plaintiff possessed the suit land for 20 years but admitted in his cross-examination that he has no land in Patia Mouza. P. W. 5 Kasimuddin stated that the plaintiff was possessing the suit land for 12/14 years. He also came from Murshidabad and admitted that he did not know about the area of the suit land. P.W.6 also came from Murshidabad. He also could not say the area and boundary of the suit land. P.Ws. 7 and 8 do not know about the suit land. 

 17. On the other hand, apart from the assertion of Kumar Begum as D.W.1 of her possession in the suit land and corrected S.A. Khatians and R.S. khatian. Ext. D series, she examined six D.Ws. in support of her possession. D.W. 2 Md. Alauddin Sarker worked as Moharer of Patia Estate and he knew the plaintiff who was a Tahsilder of Patia Raj Estate. He stated that the suit land situated surrounding the Rajbari in which the defendant No. 1 was residing since 1949. D.W.3 Kashem Ali was Peon of Paita Estate after the same was acquired by the Government. He stated that the plaintiff was a Tahsilder and defendant No.1 was possessing the suit land. In his cross-examination he further stated that he saw defendant No. 1 to catch fish from the tank. D.W. 4 Hafizur Rahman stated that his father was a Naib in the Four-annas Patia Estate. He stated that the defendant No.1 possessed the suit land. In his cross-examination he stated that he was Head Master of Buarida High School since 1973 and prior to that he was a teacher of Patia High School for six years. He seems to be a competent witness. D. W. 5 Md. Zaker Ali took lease of the tank by a registered lease deed from defendant No. 1. D.W.6 Samiruddin also took also lease of the tank from the defendant No. 1. The lease deeds were proved by them and marked as Ext. E. and E(1). D.W.7 Shajahan Ali also stated about the possession of defendant No.1. In his cross-examination he stated that he was a candidate in the last Parliament Election and sustained defeat, nevertheless he was a competent person. The learned Subordinate Judge did not sift the evidence of P.Ws and D.Ws. and jumped into the conclusion that "all the P.Ws. have deposed supporting the plaintiffs possession in the suit properties. "Upon an analysis of the oral and documentary evidence we find that plaintiff has failed to prove his possession in the suit land and consequently the suit was not maintainable in its present form being hit by the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 19. If there was conversion of Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy and his marriage with defendant No.1 and he had died as a Muslim, then Sureswari Devi did not inherit the properties of Naresh Narayan Roy. In this connection it may be pointed out that Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent has pointed out to us Ext. 14(a) the Gazette Notification dated 19.6.52 under Section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Ext. 14 the Gazette Notification dated 11.11.52 under Section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which show that the rent receiving interest and excess land was acquired by the Government from Rani Sureswari Devi, wife of late Naresh Narayan Roy of Patia. But these two Gazette Notifications relate to the rent receiving interest and non-retainable khas land of Rani Sureswari Devi. So far as the suit land is concerned. this was originally recorded in four S.A. khatians is the name of Rani Sureswari Devi but the Khatians were corrected pursuant to the orders passed by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) in Misc. Cases No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 and S.A. Khatians were corrected and subsequent R.S. Khatians were published in the name of defendant No. 11. In that view of the matter the plaintiff failed to establish that the suit land belonged to rani Sureshwari Devi from whom he claimed to have taken settlement. Thus, from the above discussions it appears to us that the plaintiff failed to establish his title and possession in the suit land; consequently the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge cannot be sustained.
